hook.line: Just a reminder that 22% of the global population uses Gmail, and this is the easiest marketing hack.
hook.visual: Dim, close selfie shot of the speaker in a branded 'COMPACT KEYWORDS' t-shirt, a three-line white sentence caption mid-frame, no cuts for the first 7 s.

beats.what: Selfie to camera with the Gmail statistic and the 'easiest hack' promise.
Phone-filmed laptop screen: dragging a logo into Gemini.
Result shown: an animated Airbnb-style logo on red, as the example of a 'minor' animation.
Converter site on the laptop: MP4 to GIF, click convert.
Zoom punch into the screen as he converts the file.
Google Account page: click the camera icon and upload the GIF.
Phone inbox with avatars, the moving icon among static ones, explaining higher open rates.
Back to selfie for a second statistic (75% of the US market) and the repeat of the promise.

why_it_works: A big statistic in the first sentence makes a tiny trick feel worth doing to a huge audience.
Each step is filmed as it happens on a real laptop, so the viewer can copy it in real time and saves the video for later.
The proof (an animated logo in a real inbox) arrives before the explanation of open rates, so the payoff is visible.
The ending repeats the opening claim, which makes the loop seamless (loop score 0.842) and encourages rewatches.
weaknesses: Dark, low-light selfie and phone-filmed screens look rough; the screen text is hard to read.
No call to action at all, so the reach does not turn into follows or comments.
The statistics change mid-video (22% global, 75% US) without a source, which can undercut trust.
for_robert: Copy the loop: end on the same claim he opened with, so the last line flows back into the first and the reel rewatches itself.
